doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Pay with Mulligan: negotiating $300 a week
summary: Raph asked for more than the usual $250 using a Broadway offer as leverage and got $300 for the European tour. He is unsure about room and meal costs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What kind of money were you making with that group?

I asked for a little more money and he paid it, and then he resented it. So we had a little tete-a-tete. At one point I was playing with Mulligan for I guess a year and he was going to go to Europe. So Nick Travis was calling the guys. He was acting as personnel manager. Nick was first trumpet player with the band. And I was offered a Broadway show, I was offered “Music Man.” It was running already but the first trombone player was leaving and the conductor wanted me to come in and play. So I had that as a springboard. That would have given me $350 a week. So I felt that instead of asking for $250, which I knew everybody more or less was getting on Gerry’s band, I asked for $300. And I got it. I wasn’t the highest paid guy by any means, but I was making a little more than two or three of the other guys in the band. So $300. I went to Europe for $300 a week, which was decent in those days.
Yeah. Did you have to pay your own way, I mean like your own meals and all that kind of stuff?

Meals yes. And oh my — I don’t remember if we paid the rooms or not. I don’t remember. I remember signing in. But I don’t remember — I have a feeling that we may have paid for the rooms, but we may have gotten an allowance. I just don’t remember that.
